title: Introduction to Operating Systems & Process Management
subtitle: OS fundamentals, system architecture, kernel, OS classifications, storage hierarchy, processes, system calls, state transitions, and schedulers.

sections.title: Operating System Fundamentals
sections.definition: A program that controls the execution of applications and acts as an intermediary between a user of a computer and the computer hardware.

roles.name: Resource Allocator
roles.description: Manages all hardware resources and decides between conflicting requests for efficient and fair resource use.

roles.name: Control Program
roles.description: Controls the execution of user programs to prevent errors and improper use of the computer.

roles.name: Kernel (Core Program)
roles.description: The one program running at all times on the computer; everything else is either a system program or an application program.

goals.description: Executes user programs and makes solving user problems easier by providing a clean interface.
Makes the computer system convenient and intuitive to use.
Uses the computer hardware in an optimal and efficient manner.
Permits effective development, testing, and introduction of new system functions without interfering with existing services.

layers_top_to_bottom.description: People, machines, or other computers interacting with the system.
Define the ways in which system resources are used to solve user computing problems (e.g., word processors, compilers, assemblers, text editors, database systems, web browsers).
Controls and coordinates the use of hardware among various applications and users.
Provides basic computing resources including CPU, memory, and I/O devices.

kernel.definition: The core part of an operating system that acts like a bridge between applications and computer hardware.
responsibilities: Translates software requests into data-processing instructions for the CPU and other electronic components.

examples_of_os.name: macOS
examples_of_os.note: Used for Apple personal computers and workstations

categories.name: Batch Operating System
categories.description: Does not interact with the computer directly. An operator takes jobs with similar requirements and groups them into batches before submitting them to the computer.
advantages: Resident monitor improves computer efficiency by eliminating idle CPU time between two consecutive jobs.
disadvantages: Lack of direct interaction between the user and the job.
CPU is often idle because mechanical I/O devices are much slower than the CPU.
Difficult to provide desired priority to urgent jobs.

categories.name: Multiprogrammed Operating System
categories.description: Keeps multiple programs in main memory (RAM) at the same time and switches the CPU to another program whenever the running program waits for an I/O operation, maximizing CPU utilization.
execution_flow: Multiple programs (P1, P2, P3, P4) are loaded into RAM.
When P1 needs an I/O operation, it enters the waiting state and CPU immediately switches to P2.
Once P1's I/O finishes, it returns to the ready queue; after P2 finishes or blocks, CPU resumes P1 until termination.
advantages: Maximizes CPU utilization so the CPU always has a job to execute.
disadvantages: Process switching takes extra overhead time and CPU scheduling is difficult (short jobs queued behind long jobs must wait).

categories.name: Time-Sharing (Multitasking) Operating System
categories.description: A logical extension of multiprogramming where many users at various terminals share a computer simultaneously. The CPU switches so frequently (response time < 1 second) that users can interact with each running program.
key_mechanisms: Each task is given an equal time slice to execute smoothly.
Uses CPU scheduling when multiple jobs are ready simultaneously.
Uses memory swapping to move processes in and out of RAM if they do not fit.
advantages: Reduces CPU idle time and maximizes resource utilization.
disadvantages: Complex and requires advanced software to schedule multiple users simultaneously.

categories.name: Distributed Operating System
categories.description: Uses multiple central processors connected through a communication network to serve multiple real-time applications and users, distributing data processing across independent nodes (each with its own CPU, memory, and disk).
advantages: Fault tolerance: if one site fails, remaining sites continue working.
Reduces processing load on individual host computers.
disadvantages: High network dependency and complex distributed synchronization.

categories.name: Network Operating System (NOS)
categories.description: Runs on a server and manages data, users, groups, security, applications, and networking functions, allowing users to share files, printers, and resources over a private network.
advantages: Centralized server management for security, file sharing, and peripheral access.
disadvantages: High cost of running and maintaining central servers; dependency on central server availability.

categories.name: Real-Time Operating System (RTOS)
categories.description: Serves real-time systems by processing and responding to inputs within a strict, very short time interval (Response Time).
advantages: Deterministic, guaranteed response within strict timing deadlines.
disadvantages: Limited multitasking flexibility and high system complexity.

concepts.name: Main Memory (RAM)
concepts.description: The only large storage media that the CPU can access directly. It provides random access and is typically volatile.

concepts.name: Secondary Memory
concepts.description: An extension of main memory that provides large, non-volatile storage capacity.

concepts.name: Caching
concepts.description: Copying information into a faster storage system on a temporary basis; main memory itself can be viewed as a fast cache for secondary storage.

tradeoffs.moving_up: Increases speed and cost per bit.
tradeoffs.moving_down: Increases storage capacity and access time.

definitions.program: A passive entity stored on a disk as an executable file containing a set of instructions to perform a specific task.
definitions.process: A program in execution. It is an active entity whose execution progresses in a sequential manner.

comparison.program: Stored on secondary storage (disk) as an executable file
comparison.process: Loaded into main memory (RAM) for execution
A dynamic program currently in execution

system_calls.definition: The programming interfaces through which a user program requests services from the operating system kernel.

states.name: New
states.description: The initial state when a process is being created by the OS while the program resides in secondary memory. The OS prepares necessary resources before admitting it.

states.name: Ready
states.description: The process is loaded into RAM and is ready to execute, waiting for the CPU to become available. Controlled by the Long-Term Scheduler (LTS).

states.name: Running
states.description: Instructions are currently being executed by the CPU. Selected from the ready queue by the Short-Term Scheduler (STS) and assigned via the dispatcher.

states.name: Waiting / Blocked
states.description: The process cannot continue execution until an external event or I/O operation completes, after which it returns to the Ready state.

states.name: Terminated
states.description: The process has finished execution or been stopped by the OS, and all allocated memory and resources are de-allocated.

states.name: Suspend Wait
states.description: A process waiting for an event or I/O operation that has been temporarily swapped out from RAM to secondary storage by the Mid-Term Scheduler (MTS).

states.name: Suspend Ready
states.description: A process that is ready to execute but has been temporarily swapped out from RAM to secondary storage; must be brought back into RAM before running.

transitions.trigger: Time quantum expired or higher-priority preemption (Multitasking)
Swapped out to backing store by Mid-Term Scheduler (MTS)
I/O completes while still in secondary storage
Resumed / swapped back into RAM by MTS
Swapped out to free RAM by MTS

schedulers.name: Short-Term Scheduler
schedulers.primary_role: Selects which process in the ready queue gets the CPU next.
schedulers.control_metric: Controls CPU allocation and fast context switching.

schedulers.name: Mid-Term Scheduler
schedulers.primary_role: Moves processes in and out of main memory (swapping between RAM and backing store).
schedulers.control_metric: Controls process suspension and reduces memory contention.

schedulers.name: Long-Term Scheduler
schedulers.primary_role: Selects which new processes enter main memory (Ready queue) from secondary storage.
